draft.change: Add the feminine noun זֵעָה under יזע with the sense “sweat” for Genesis 3:19, correcting the supplied gloss “dry ground.”
draft.definition: Sweat that forms on the body during exertion.
draft.evidence: Genesis 3:19 locates the sweat on the worker’s face as he labors for bread.

analysis.evidence: אַפֶּיךָ completes the construct phrase בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּיךָ, “by the sweat of your face.” The phrase modifies תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם, “you shall eat bread,” describing the exertion required to obtain food. The ground is named separately later in the verse as הָאֲדָמָה.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ (by, with) + feminine singular construct noun זֵעַת (sweat of).
analysis.sense: Perspiration on the face during physical exertion.

analysis.evidence: בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּיךָ means “by the sweat of your face.” The sweat on the addressee’s face conveys the toil required to obtain bread.
analysis.morphology: Masculine dual noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: (dual) face, above all bowed to the ground

analysis.evidence: לֶחֶם (“bread”) is the direct object of תֹּאכַל. The masculine singular suffix in אַפֶּיךָ (“your face”) confirms that the verb addresses the man directly.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular, with preformative ת־

analysis.evidence: לֶחֶם is the direct object of תֹּאכַל, “you will eat.” Eating bread by the sweat of one’s brow until one returns to the ground presents bread as the food that sustains life.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַד שׁוּבְךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה means “until you return to the ground.” The return marks the endpoint of eating bread by the sweat of your brow.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected preposition without prefix or suffix, governing the infinitive construct שׁוּבְךָ.

analysis.evidence: עַד שׁוּבְךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה means “until you return to the ground.” The next clause says that the man was taken from the ground, and וְאֶל עָפָר תָּשׁוּב repeats the verb with the same subject and destination, “and to dust you will return.”
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with the second-person masculine singular suffix ־ךָ as its subject.
analysis.sense: return to one’s place of origin

analysis.evidence: In שׁוּבְךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה, “your return to the ground,” אֶל marks the ground as the destination of the return.

The man will return to the ground because he was taken from it (מִמֶּנָּה לֻקָּחְתָּ). The parallel statement that he is dust and will return to dust identifies the ground as the source of his bodily substance.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: earth, as the stuff things are made of

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for returning to the ground. In מִמֶּנָּה לֻקָּחְתָּ (“from it you were taken”), the suffix on מִמֶּנָּה refers back to הָאֲדָמָה (“the ground”).

מִמֶּנָּה means “from it” and refers to הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground.” The man will return to the ground because he was taken from it. The following words, “you are dust,” identify the ground as his material source.
analysis.morphology: Passive perfect (traditionally parsed as Pual), second masculine singular, with the ending ־תָּ.

analysis.evidence: The second כִּי introduces the reason for the return to the ground. עָפָר אַתָּה means “you are dust,” and וְאֶל־עָפָר תָּשׁוּב continues “and to dust you will return.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עָפָר אַתָּה, “you are dust,” עָפָר is the predicate of אַתָּה. The preceding words say that the man was taken from the ground, identifying dust as the material of his origin.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי עָפָר אַתָּה, “for you are dust,” אַתָּה is the subject and עָפָר is the predicate identifying what the man is. The next clause repeats עָפָר in “and to dust you will return.”
analysis.morphology: Independent second-person masculine singular pronoun, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: you (are): the one addressed named or identified

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶל עָפָר תָּשׁוּב, “and to dust you will return,” עָפָר names the material to which the man returns at death. The earlier phrase אֶל הָאֲדָמָה, “to the ground,” identifies that destination, and כִּי עָפָר אַתָּה, “for you are dust,” explains the return.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶל־עָפָר תָּשׁוּב means “and to dust you will return.” It echoes the earlier statement that the addressee will return to the ground from which he was taken.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular
analysis.sense: return to one’s place of origin
